paragraphs.text: Spotlight-style command palette for DeepSeek Harness: settings, plugins, sessions, keyboard shortcut
s, themes, and any registered command.
# dsh-spotlight

One shortcut, everything at your fingertips. Press `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P` anywhere,
or `/` outside a tex

t field, to summon a Spotlight-style palette for
DeepSeek Harness — launch
pages, panels, sessions,
themes, and any command other plugins register, in seconds.
English | 中文
Dark theme
## What it does

- **Global palette.** One overlay entry in `shell.overlay`, opened by keyboard
or by any registered

command.
- **First-class commands.** Settings, Plugins, Search Sessions, Add Workspace,
Keyboard Sho

rtcuts, New Session, Archive Current Session, Compact Session,
Toggle Sidebar, Toggle Right Sidebar,

Workspace Files, theme (dark / light /
system), and language (English / 中文).
- **Settings deep link

s.** Every settings section becomes a `Settings → Section`
command (Settings → General, Settings → M

odels, …) that opens the panel
directly on that tab. The section catalog mirrors the shell's
`settin

gs.section` slot and refreshes with it, including sections registered
by other plugins. When the she

ll's store handle is unreachable, the command
falls back to opening Settings and clicking the sectio

n's nav cell.
- **Shortcut mirror.** Every remaining configurable shell shortcut appears in a
**Shor

tcuts** group with its effective keycaps. Running one goes through the
shell's own shortcut resoluti

on, so rename, fork, split, fullscreen, terminal,
and future feature commands participate without pl

ugin-specific wiring.
Window/page close and delete/remove actions are deliberately excluded.
- **Ext

ensible registry.** Other client plugins contribute commands through the
`spotlight` service. Titles

, groups, keywords, and hints are searchable in
English and Chinese.
- **Owned resources.** The styl

esheet is injected during bundle materialization
and claimed by the module system; the locale dictio

nary, command registry,
shortcut entries, and overlay slot are registered as Cordis effects, so
disa
ble / HMR teardown removes them.
## Requirements

| DeepSeek Harness | `0.2.x` (developed and verified against `0.2.1-rc.5`) |
| Surface | Web client

(`dsh-web-app`) or the desktop app |
| Node.js | not needed for the plugin itself; the test suite ru

ns on Node 20+ |
| Build | none — the browser bundle is hand-written JavaScript |
## Install

The package is a DSH **bundle**: `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch` and
`dsh.client`, and `c
ordis.patch.yml` inserts the host row.
### From GitHub
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Omit `#v1.0.3` to track the default branch.
### From a local checkout
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The installer must leave `dsh-spotlight` in the profile's
`dsh.profile.bundles` list, not only in `d

ependencies`. A dependency without a
bundle selection never composes the host row, so the client hal

f never reaches
the module graph.

**Restart the application after installing or updating.** The host half is a
Node module and the run

ning process keeps the module generation it already
loaded; the client module graph also snapshots e

ach bundle before publication,
so a page reload alone can keep serving the previous bundle. A restar

t
guarantees the new client half and re-registers the palette shortcut with the
native keyboard brid

uarantees the new client half and re-registers the palette shortcut with the
native keyboard bridge.
## How it works

- **Host half** (`index.js`) is a no-op Cordis row. Its only job is to make the
package a loader ent

ry; the client half is what users see.
- **Client half** (`client.js`) is one `window.__ModuleLoader

__.load({ id,
factory })` module. It requires only `react` from the shared platform table.
- **One s

tylesheet.** The CSS is inserted during bundle materialization and
claimed by the module system (`da

ta-plugin-css`), so disable/HMR teardown
removes it without a manual listener.
- **One overlay slot.

** The palette registers into `shell.overlay` and returns
`null` while closed, so it costs one inert

slot entry when unused.
- **Owned effects.** Locale dictionaries, built-in commands, the `spotlight

`
service, the keyboard listener, and the shortcut registrations all live in
`ctx.effect`, which mak

es repeated apply/dispose safe.
- **Shortcut registration.** `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P` is a normal `ctx.sho

rtcuts`
command. The service may mount after this plugin, so registration waits with
`ctx.inject(['s

hortcuts'], ...)` instead of racing `ctx.get()`.
- **Shortcut mirror.** The palette subscribes to `c

tx.shortcuts.catalog`,
mirrors its non-curated rows into a **Shortcuts** group, and invokes a row vi

a
the shell registry. Web keeps a synthetic-key fallback for versions where
that registry is unavail

shell registry. Web keeps a synthetic-key fallback for versions where
that registry is unavailable.

No build step, no runtime dependencies, and no imports from `@deepseek-ai/*`
packages: a third-party
plugin cannot resolve the DSH package tree at runtime.
## Compatibility and limits

- The bare `/` opener is a raw capture listener because the shortcut service
rejects modifier-less d

efaults; it is not rebindable. `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P` is
the normal, rebindable command.
- The legacy `C

md/Ctrl+Shift+/` listener remains as a convenience where the OS
delivers the event (Windows/Linux);

macOS consumes it for Help menu search.
- The **Shortcuts** mirror calls `ctx.shortcuts.registry.inv

oke()`, an internal
member of the shortcut service rather than a documented public API. Every
step i

s guarded. If the registry is absent, Web replays the effective
binding and Desktop keeps only the f

irst-class commands.
- A mirrored command runs through the shell's own `resolve()` and can be
blocke

d without a current session, focused page, or idle agent. The palette
closes before the command runs

and does not show a blocked reason.
- **Compact Session** requires an idle agent; the Host's refusa

l is logged to
the browser console.
- Window/page close and delete/remove actions are excluded from

the mirror.
- Empty groups render no heading; commands without a group/title fall back to
their id.

- The palette is keyboard-first, but the list is not a full ARIA combobox; it
exposes a dialog, a li
stbox, and option roles.
